content:
In #43184 (test PR for the issue) I added two instances SeminormedGroup.toESeminormedMonoid and SeminormedCommGroup.toESeminormedCommMonoid (and their additive versions). The reason I did that was that I wanted to generalize MeasureTheory.Filtration.memLp_limitProcess_of_eLpNorm_bdd to a SeminormedAddGroup F (just for the sake of generalization in passing) and I realized that there was no instance synthesis from SeminormedAddGroup to ESeminormedMonoid, which is needed in the proof. By doing so however, the proof of MeasureTheory.integral_of_ae_eq_zero_or_one now fails. It is easily fixable, but I don't get why it fails. In this proof the lemma MeasureTheory.Integrable.smul_measure is used inside rw, and rw does not manage to see through the defeq X ⁻¹' {1} and {ω | X ω = 1}.

I am not very knowledgeable about how to investigate such bugs, but it seems to me that everything should be defeq and I don't understand what is going on at all. Simply adding the explicit shape of the constant X ⁻¹' {1} solves it.
rw works up to syntactic equality, not definitional equality.
I know that, but what is strange is that the proof works without the (seemingly unrelated) instance change.

Different ones inferred? As in, the initial statement had a One from the AddGroup, but then changes to the one from EMonoid, and that's how the One instances don't match anymore syntactically. Perhaps there is some instance flattening which would avoid this.

AFAICT the instances are the same everywhere. Actually I would not expect the original proof to work so it is quite puzzling. I guess this is a good example of why complicated proofs should be avoided inside rw.

Claude Opus 5 says (and I didn't check):

Short version

rw never saw through X ⁻¹' {1} ≡ {ω | X ω = 1}. It can't: rw's kabstract
matches only up to instances transparency, and Set.preimage is a plain def. On
master the rewrite works because the measure it's matching against is still a
metavariable at match time. Your instances change the elaboration order so
that it isn't one any more.

The evidence

1. rw cannot match those two forms — today, on master:

lean
example {Ω : Type} (X : Ω → ℝ) (f : Set Ω → ℕ) (g : ℕ → ℕ)
(h : g (f {ω | X ω = 1}) = 0) : g (f (X ⁻¹' {1})) = 0 := by
rw [h] -- Did not find an occurrence of the pattern
(and {ω | X ω = 1} = X ⁻¹' {1} is not provable by with_reducible rfl).

2. What the pattern actually is. Make the rw fail on purpose (... at hXmeas)
and look at the reported pattern.

- master: ∫ (x : ?m.96), ?m.103 x ∂(?m.101 + ?m.102) — both measures are
metavariables.

- your branch (from the CI log of the failing build): ∫ (x : ?m.108), ?m.114 x
∂(?m.101 + μ {ω | X ω = 1} • ?m.110).

So on master the whole Integrable … argument is postponed by the elaborator;
?ν gets assigned by matching against the goal (μ (X ⁻¹' {1}) • dirac 1), and
Integrable.smul_measure _ h is only elaborated afterwards, against that
now-concrete type. That check runs at default transparency, where μ (X ⁻¹'
{1}) ≠ ∞ and h : ¬μ {ω | X ω = 1} = ⊤ are happily defeq. On your branch the
argument is elaborated first, so c := μ {ω | X ω = 1} is read off h and ends
up in the pattern — and now the keyed match has to do the set defeq at
instances transparency, which it can't.

3. Why your instances flip that. Integrable takes [ContinuousENorm ε]. On
master, for ℝ that instance is the constant

@SeminormedAddGroup.toContinuousENorm ℝ …

which is what sits in the Integrable hypotheses of integral_add_measure. But
Integrable.smul_measure is stated with [ESeminormedAddMonoid ε], so its
conclusion carries @ESeminormedAddMonoid.toContinuousENorm ?ε _ ?inst — a
projection out of an instance metavariable. Unifying that against a different
constant is stuck, so the elaborator gives up on the argument for now and
postpones it. Your PR removes SeminormedGroup.toContinuousENorm in favour of
SeminormedGroup.toESeminormedMonoid, so the instance in the goal is now itself
headed by ESeminormedAddMonoid.toContinuousENorm; unification becomes
first-order, succeeds immediately, and nothing gets postponed.

I checked that this is really the trigger without building your branch: on
current master, replace .smul_measure by an otherwise identical copy stated
with [NormedAddCommGroup ε] (so its instance term is the same constant as the
goal's), and you get your error verbatim:

lean
theorem Integrable.smul_measure' {α ε : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α]
[NormedAddCommGroup ε]
{μ : Measure α} {f : α → ε} (h : Integrable f μ) {c : ℝ≥0∞} (hc : c ≠ ∞) :
Integrable f (c • μ) := h.smul_measure hc
-- ... rw [integral_add_measure ⟨…⟩ <| .smul_measure' (by simp
[integrable_dirac]) h]
-- Did not find an occurrence of the pattern
-- ∫ (x : ?m.108), ?m.113 x ∂(?m.101 + μ {ω | X ω = 1} • ?m.112)

Fixes

- What you did — writing by_cases h : μ (X ⁻¹' {1}) = ⊤ — is the right fix: it
makes the pattern syntactically match.

- rw (transparency := .default) [integral_add_measure …] also works
(verified), since then Set.preimage unfolds during matching.

Nothing is wrong with the new instances; the old proof was relying on an
elaboration-order accident. The general moral is worth flagging: when a lemma
is generalised to a weaker class, the instance in its statement turns into a
projection out of a metavariable, and that changes when arguments get
elaborated — which silently changes what ends up in a rw pattern.
